Rashi on Meilah 8b:10:1.hebrew: להכי כתיב והנשאר לכדתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל שאם נשאר - כלומר, אם נשאר מן הדם — מצוה לעשות מיצוי; אבל אם לא נשאר — לא מעכב, דמיצוי אינו מעכב:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:10:1.english: For this reason it is written "and the remainder" as the baraita of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: "that if [blood] remains" - That is, if some of the blood remains, there is a commandment to perform squeezing; but if none remains, it does not prevent [validity], for squeezing is not essential.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:10:2.hebrew: ומאי חטאת היא - לאו כדקא בעית למימר דאומרוהנשאר ימצה קאי, דליהוי משמע דבשיריים, דהיינו מיצוי, הוי עיקר חטאת, דמיצוי מעכב:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:10:2.english: And what is "it is a sin offering"? - [It is] not as you wished to say, that it refers to "and the remainder shall be squeezed out," so that it would imply that through the remainders, that is, the squeezing, the essence of the sin offering is achieved, because the squeezing is indispensable.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:10:3.hebrew: אלא ארישיה דקרא קאי - דכתיב אוהזה מדם החטאת באצבעו, חטאת היא, לומר דהזאה מעכבת ולא מיצוי:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:10:3.english: Rather, it refers to the beginning of the verse - [The verse states:] "And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering with his finger"; "it is a sin offering" — to say that the sprinkling is indispensable, but the squeezing [out of the remaining blood] is not.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:11:1.hebrew: ה"נ שאם ניתותר - שכשקמץ את המנחה, אם ניתותר, דאיכא שיריים — למצוה, שפיר; ואם לא ניתותר, כגון שאם חסרו שיריים בין קמיצה להקטרה — לית לן בה:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:11:1.english: Indeed, that if some remains - That when [the priest] took the handful from the meal offering, if some remained, so that there are remainders, [this is] a mitzvah, and it is good; but if none remained, [for example] if the remainders were lost between the taking of the handful and the burning, we have no concern with it:

Rashi on Meilah 8b:11:2.hebrew: וכי תימא הכי נמי - דשיריים לא מעכבי. והתניא: "מסלתה ומשמנה" — דמצי למיכתב קרא "מסלת ומשמן", מאי "מסלתה ומשמנה"? שיהא כל סלתה ושמנה קיים, ואפילו שיריים, דהכי משמע "מסלתה" — מן הסלת שהיה בשעת קמיצה, שהיה כולו. אלמא דחסרון שיריים מעכבי (גבי שיריים נמי אמרינן דחסרון שיריים מעכב), והיכי אמרינן שאם לא ניתותר לא מעכב:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:11:2.english: And if you would say: Indeed so - that the remainders do not impede [the offering]. But it was taught in a baraita: "Of its fine flour and of its oil" — for the verse could have written "of fine flour and of oil"; what is [the meaning of] "of its fine flour and of its oil"? That all of its fine flour and its oil must be intact, even the remainders. For this is what "of its fine flour" implies: from the fine flour that existed at the time of the removal of the handful, [when] it was all [there]. Evidently, a deficiency in the remainders impedes [the offering] (with regard to the remainders too, we say that a deficiency in the remainders impedes); so how can we say that if none is left over, it does not impede?

Rashi on Meilah 8b:2:1.hebrew: רבי מאיר אומר מטמא את הקדש - דהוא שני, ומשוי לקדש שלישי:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:2:1.english: Rabbi Meir says: He renders sacrificial food impure - For he is [impure in the] second [degree], and he makes the sacrificial food third [degree].

Rashi on Meilah 8b:2:2.hebrew: וחכ"א כשם שפוסל כו' - אבל טמויי לא מטמא, והיינו כמתניתין:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:2:2.english: And the Sages say: Just as he disqualifies, etc. - But he does not render [anything] impure; and this is [the same as] our mishnah.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:3:1.hebrew: אמר רבא לאבא שאול - נמי, דאמר תחלה לקדש דקעביד לקדש שני, מיתרצא נמי מתני'. דודאי טבול יום מדאורייתא פוסל ואינו מטמא, ורבנן עשו מעלה בקדשים, דהוה טבול יום תחלה לקדש, דהוי כי אוכל ראשון ועושה שני. ומתני' בדאורייתא קתני, דאינו אלא פוסל:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:3:1.english: Rava said: According to Abba Shaul - too, who said [that a tevul yom is] a first[-degree impurity] with regard to sacred [items], in that he makes sacred [food] a second[-degree impurity], the mishna is also resolved. For certainly, by Torah law, a tevul yom disqualifies [food] but does not render it impure; and the Sages established a higher standard with regard to consecrated items, so that a tevul yom is a first[-degree impurity] with regard to sacred [food], as he is like a first[-degree] food that makes [another] a second. And the mishna teaches [its law] according to Torah law, that he only disqualifies [it].

Rashi on Meilah 8b:4:1.hebrew: לר"מ - נמי מיתרצא מתני', דהאי דקאמר התנא מטמא את הקדש, דעביד ליה שלישי, ופוסל את התרומה מדרבנן. אבל מדאורייתא, אינו אלא פוסל מאחר שטבל:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:4:1.english: According to Rabbi Meir - The Mishnah is also resolved, [for] that which [the Tanna] says that he renders the consecrated item impure [means] that he makes it a third[-degree impurity], and he disqualifies terumah by rabbinic law. But by Torah law, he only disqualifies [it], since he has immersed.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:4:2.hebrew: ורבנן - דאמרי: כשם שפוסל וכו', ולא אמרי דמטמא. קסברי: כיון דטבל, קלשא ליה טומאה, דפסול משוי, ולא טמא:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:4:2.english: And the Rabbis - who say: Just as he disqualifies, etc., yet they do not say that he renders [it] impure. They hold: Since he has immersed, his impurity is weakened, so that he renders [it] disqualified, but not impure.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:5:1.hebrew: הא איסורא איכא - כלומר, איסור אכילה:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:5:1.english: But there is a prohibition - That is to say, the prohibition of eating [it].

Rashi on Meilah 8b:5:2.hebrew: ואמאי הא ממונא דכהנים הוא - מאחר שהוזה דמה, שהותרה להם באכילה:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:5:2.english: But why? Isn't it the property of the priests - Since its blood was sprinkled, [the meat] was permitted to them for eating.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:6:1.hebrew: א"ר חנינא ליוצא - כלומר, מתניתין מדברת שיצא, דהתם איכא איסור אכילה. ורבי עקיבא הוא דאמר זריקה מועלת ליוצא, לאפוקיה מידי מעילה, או לשריפה, כדאמרינן לעיל. אבל לאו בת אכילה היא, כדאמרינן בסוף פירקין: "אבל לאכילה לא מרצה". הא הזאה, נהי דמהניא לאפוקיה מידי מעילה, אבל להתיר היוצא באכילה לא מהניא. והיינו דקא דייק "אבל איסורא איכא", דלאו בת אכילה היא:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:6:1.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said: [It refers] to an item that went out - That is, [the mishna speaks of an item] that went out [of its permitted place], for there there is a prohibition of eating. And it is Rabbi Akiva who said that sprinkling is effective for an item that went out, to remove it from the status of misuse, or [to render it fit] for burning, as we said above. But it is not fit for eating, as we say at the end of the chapter: "But for eating it does not appease." That is, the sprinkling, although it helps to remove it from [the law of] misuse, does not help to permit the item that went out to be eaten. And this is why [the Gemara] infers "but there is a prohibition," because it is not fit for eating.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:7:1.hebrew: אמר רב הונא אמר רב מיצוי דחטאת העוף - דכתיב והנשאר בדם ימצה, ולאחר הזאה ימצה:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:7:1.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said: The squeezing of a bird sin offering - For it is written (Leviticus 5:9), "And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out"; it is squeezed out after the sprinkling.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:7:2.hebrew: אינו מעכב - דכיון דהוזה, אע"פ שלא מיצה, נעשית מצותו, ויצא מידי מעילה, וחייבין עליו משום נותר וטמא, ויצא נמי ידי חובתו, והיינו דאינו מעכב הכפרה:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:7:2.english: It does not invalidate - For since [the blood] was sprinkled, even though he did not squeeze [it out], its mitzvah was performed, and it left the category of *me'ilah* [misuse of consecrated property], and one is liable for it on account of *notar* [leftover] and [for eating it while] impure; and he also fulfilled his obligation, [meaning] that it does not prevent the atonement.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:7:3.hebrew: דתני רב הוזה דמה - דמדקתני במתניתין גבי חטאת העוף "הוזה דמה", ולא קתני "מיצה דמה", אלמא ס"ל לתנא דמתני' דהזאה עיקר, ומיצוי לא מעכב:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:7:3.english: For Rav taught "its blood was sprinkled" - For since the mishna teaches regarding a bird sin offering "its blood was sprinkled," and does not teach "its blood was squeezed out," it is evident that the Tanna of the mishna holds that sprinkling is the essential [act], and squeezing out does not invalidate.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:8:1.hebrew: ורב אדא בר אהבה אמר משמיה דרב מיצוי מעכב - דלא יצא ידי חובתו, ולא נתכפר, ולא הוקבע החטאת בפיגול ונותר וטמא, אע"פ שהוזה, עד דעביד מיצוי:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:8:1.english: And Rav Adda bar Ahava said in the name of Rav: Squeezing out [the blood] is indispensable - For [the owner] has not fulfilled his obligation, and has not been atoned for, and the sin offering is not established [as subject to the laws of] piggul, notar, and impurity, even though [its blood] was sprinkled, until he performs the squeezing out.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:8:2.hebrew: ותני רב מיצה דמה - במתני' גבי חטאת העוף קתני "מיצה דמה", ולא קתני "הוזה דמה", דס"ל דמיצוי נמי עיקר מצוה הויא, ומעכב:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:8:2.english: And Rav teaches: "Its blood was squeezed out" - In the Mishnah, regarding the bird sin offering, it teaches "its blood was squeezed out," and it does not teach "its blood was sprinkled," because he holds that squeezing out is also an essential part of the commandment, and it is indispensable [to the atonement].

Rashi on Meilah 8b:9:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרב אדא היינו דכתיב והנשאר בדם ימצה אל יסוד המזבח וגו' - דההוא דנשאר אחר הזאה, דהיינו מיצוי, איקרי חטאת. אלמא דשיריים, דהיינו מיצוי, מעכב:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:9:1.english: Granted, according to Rav Adda, this is as it is written: "And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out at the base of the altar," etc. - For that [blood] which remains after the sprinkling, which is the squeezing out, is called a sin offering. Evidently, the remainder [of the blood], which is the squeezing out, is essential.

Rashi on Meilah 8b:9:2.hebrew: אלא לרב הונא - דאמר מיצוי לא מעכב, מאי "והנשאר"? כיון דלא מעכב, ל"ל דכתיב "והנשאר"?:
Rashi on Meilah 8b:9:2.english: But according to Rav Huna - who says that squeezing out [the blood] is not essential, what is [the meaning of] "and the remainder"? Since it is not essential, why do I need [the verse] that writes "and the remainder"?

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:10:1.hebrew: כדתניא דבי רבי ישמעאל שאם נשאר - פי' אם נשאר — ימצה, ואם לאו — לא ימצה, וליכא עיכובא:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:10:1.english: As it is taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael: "That if there remains" - Explanation: If [blood] remains, he squeezes it out; and if not, he does not squeeze it out, and there is no [case of the offering's] being invalidated.

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:10:2.hebrew: ומאי חטאת היא ארישא - כלומר: לא קאי "חטאת היא" אמיצוי, אלא קאי ארישא דקרא, דהיינו הזאה ושאר ענייני מליקה שכתובים קודם "והנשאר":
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:10:2.english: "And what is 'it is a sin offering'? It refers to the first clause" - That is: "It is a sin offering" does not refer to the squeezing out, but rather refers to the first part of the verse, namely the sprinkling and the other matters of *melikah* that are written earlier, before "and the remainder."

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:11:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה גבי מנחה דכתיב והנותרת ה"נ שאם ניתותר - כלומר: גבי מנחה דכתיב "והנותרת מן המנחה יאכלו אהרן ובניו" ה"נ שאם ניתותר יאכלו, ואם לא ניתותרו השיריים בין קמיצה להקטרה — אין בכך כלום. וכ"ת ה"נ, והא תניא "מסלתה" וכו' — משמע הכא דפשיטא ליה להש"ס שיריים שחסרו בין קמיצה להקטרה פסול. וקשיא: דפ"ק דמנחות (דף ט.) פליגי רבי יוחנן ור"ל, וקסבר חד מינייהו דמקטיר קומץ עליה. וי"ל דנהי דמקטיר קומץ עליה, מ"מ מודה שאותן השיריים אסורין באכילה, כדמשמע לישנא ד"והנותרת מן המנחה יאכלו" וכו', דכי לא ניתותר (כלום) [כלומר] שחסרו השיריים — לא אכלו כהנים:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:11:1.english: "If so, with regard to a meal offering, where it is written 'But that which is left' — so too, that if some is left" - That is: With regard to a meal offering, where it is written, "But that which is left of the meal offering shall be eaten by Aaron and his sons" — so too [it would mean] that if some is left, they eat it, but if none of the remainder was left between the removal of the handful and its burning, it is of no consequence. And if you say: So too [that is the case] — but it was taught: "Of its fine flour" etc. — it implies here that it was obvious to the Talmud that if the remainders were diminished between the removal of the handful and the burning, [the offering] is invalid. And this is difficult: for in the first chapter of Menachot (9a), Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish disagree, and one of them holds that he burns the handful over it. And one can say that granted that he burns the handful over it, nevertheless he agrees that those remainders are forbidden to be eaten, as the wording "But that which is left of the meal offering shall be eaten" etc. implies, for when none was left (at all) [that is,] [meaning] that the remainders were diminished — the priests do not eat [it]:

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:1:1.hebrew: תחלה לקדש - ואם נגע באוכל קדש, עושה אותו שני, ושני — שלישי, ושלישי — רביעי:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:1:1.english: A first[-degree impurity] with regard to sacred [food] - And if he touched sacred food, he makes it a second[-degree impurity]; and a second makes [another item] a third, and a third makes [another] a fourth:

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:2:1.hebrew: מטמא את הקדש - לעשות עוד אחר, ופוסל התרומה — שלא תעשה יותר:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:2:1.english: He renders sacrificial food impure - so that it makes yet another [item impure]; and he disqualifies the teruma — so that it will not make [any] more [items impure]:

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:2:2.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים [כו'] כך הוא פוסל כו' - דקא סברי דטבול יום אינו רק פוסל בשום דבר, ואף במשקה קדש; וכוותייהו מוקי מתניתין:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:2:2.english: "And the Rabbis say… so too he disqualifies, etc." - For they hold that a tevul yom only disqualifies, but does not render anything impure, and [this applies] even to sacred liquids; and [the Gemara] establishes the mishna in accordance with their view:

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:3:1.hebrew: לאבא שאול מעלה עשו בקדשים כו' - וא"ת: הכא משמע דטבול יום מדרבנן הוא, כדקאמר: "שוינהו רבנן לטבול יום וכו'". ובסוטה פרק כשם (דף כט:) יליף רביעי בקדש מק"ו ממחוסר כפורים: ומה מחוסר כפורים שאין פסול בתרומה — פוסל בקודש, שלישי שפסול בתרומה אינו דין שיעשה רביעי בקדש? ופריך: אוכל הבא מחמת טבול יום יוכיח. ומשני: דילמא סבר לה כאבא שאול. ומאי קאמר? הא דאבא שאול דרבנן הוא! וצ"ל דרביעי בקדש דרבנן הוא. וכן פי' רש"י בפרק קמא דפסחים (דף יט.), דלא (חשיב) [משכחת] ליה רביעי בקדש למ"ד אין אוכל מטמא אוכל אלא מדרבנן הוא. מיהו ר"ת פי' דמשכחת ליה ע"י עצים, ורביעי בקדש דאורייתא (ואבא שאול ה"ק ליה). היכי קאמר "דילמא סבר לה כאבא שאול", והא דאבא שאול מדרבנן הוא? וי"ל דסוגיא דסוטה (דף כט:) לית ליה הא דרבא, אלא אית ליה דטבול יום מן התורה, וכדבעא הש"ס הכא לומר דמתני' רבנן היא:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:3:1.english: "According to Abba Shaul, they established a higher standard with regard to consecrated items," etc. - And if you ask: Here it implies that [the status of] a tevul yom is rabbinic, as [Rava] said: "The Sages equated a tevul yom," etc. Yet in Sotah, chapter "Keshem" (29b), [the Gemara] derives [the existence of] a fourth-degree [impurity] in sacred food by a kal vachomer from one who lacks atonement: If one who lacks atonement, [whose status] does not disqualify terumah, disqualifies sacred food, then a third-degree [impurity], which does disqualify terumah, should it not be that it makes a fourth-degree [impurity] in sacred food? And [the Gemara] challenges: Food that came into contact with a tevul yom will prove [otherwise]. And it answers: Perhaps he holds like Abba Shaul. But what is it saying? That [position] of Abba Shaul is rabbinic! [So] one must say that a fourth-degree [impurity] in sacred food is rabbinic. And so Rashi explained in the first chapter of Pesachim (19a), that one does not find a fourth-degree [impurity] in sacred food according to the one who says that food does not impart impurity to food except by rabbinic law. However, Rabbeinu Tam explained that one can find it through wood, and [that] a fourth-degree [impurity] in sacred food is by Torah law (and Abba Shaul is saying this to him). How can [the Gemara] say "perhaps he holds like Abba Shaul," when [the ruling] of Abba Shaul is rabbinic? And one can say that the passage in Sotah (29b) does not hold this [statement] of Rava, but rather holds that [the impurity of] a tevul yom is from the Torah, and as the Gemara here wished to say, that the Mishnah is [in accordance with] the Rabbis:

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:7:1.english: And Rav taught: "Its blood was sprinkled" - For as soon as the blood of a bird sin offering has been sprinkled, its commandment is completed; we read [of it] (etc.):

Tosafot on Meilah 8b:9:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרב אדא בר אהבה היינו דכתיב והנשאר בדם ימצה - אע"ג דנשאר, חטאת היא. כלומר, אע"ג דאין דם אלא מה שנשאר מן ההזאה, עדיין היא חטאת, ותלויה הזייתה במיצוי שהוא מעכב:
Tosafot on Meilah 8b:9:1.english: Granted, according to Rav Adda bar Ahava, this is as it is written: "And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out" - Even though [it is only what] remains, it is a sin offering. That is to say, even though there is no blood [left] other than what remains from the sprinkling, it is still a sin offering, and its sprinkling is dependent on the squeezing out, which is essential:
